extracted.intended_audience: immigration stakeholders (petitioners/employers), surety companies, immigration practitioners, small-entity representatives, and public commenters on DHS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply the regulatory criteria and procedural requirements in DHS's proposed public-charge rulemaking (IRFA, NEPA, PRA, bond process, forms changes) for notice-and-comment and compliance analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory minimum factors for public charge determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 212(a)(4) of the Act, 8 U.S.C. 1182(a)(4), the statute requires DHS to consider the following minimum factors that reflect the likelihood that an alien will become a public charge: the alien’s age; health; family status; assets, resources, and financial status; and education and skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, DHS may consider any affidavit of support submitted by the alien’s sponsor and any other factors relevant to the likelihood of the alien becoming a public charge. The proposed rule also would establish enhanced evidentiary requirements and USCIS discretion to request Form I-944 to determine likelihood of receipt of public benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for extension/change of status (EOS/COS) regarding public benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-receipt of public benefits and being unlikely to receive public benefits in the future is a condition of EOS/COS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS, at its discretion, may request the applicant to file a Form I-944 to determine likelihood of receipt of public benefits in the future. This condition is reflected in updates to forms such as I-129, I-129CW, I-539, and others listed in the PRA table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge bond process (posting and cancellation criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed provisions establish a public charge bond process (Form I-945) and allow either an alien or an obligor (individual or entity, including surety companies) to request cancellation of a public bond using Form I-356.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation may be requested because the alien has permanently departed the United States, naturalized, or died, or following the alien’s fifth anniversary of admission to the United States as a lawful permanent resident, or if the alien obtains an immigration status that is exempt from the public charge ground of inadmissibility. DHS estimates filing volumes and notes a Form I-356 request includes a time burden of 15 minutes and a $25 DHS fee; obligors may pass costs to aliens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) — required element: reasons for action
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. A description of the reasons why the action by the agency is being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS must explain why the regulatory action is considered; in this rule DHS explains it seeks to better ensure applicants are self-sufficient and minimize burden on the safety net.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) — required element: objectives and legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: 2. A succinct statement of the objectives of, and legal basis for, the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states objectives and identifies legal authority in the preamble; IRFA must tie the rule's objectives to applicable statutes and legal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) — required element: number of small entities affected
rubrics_metrics.description: 3. A description and, where feasible, an estimate of the number of small entities to which the proposed changes would apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS provides estimates (e.g., 336,335 beneficiaries via Form I-129 annually; 6,307 via I-129CW), discusses inability to estimate RFEs or exact small-entity counts for surety companies, and invites public comment and data on numbers of small entities affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) — required element: reporting/recordkeeping/compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 4. A description of the projected reporting, recordkeeping, and other compliance requirements of the proposed rule, including an estimate of the classes of small entities that will be subject to the requirement and the types of professional skills necessary for preparation of the report or record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS describes time burdens (e.g., additional 30 minutes for petitioners filing I-129 or I-129CW; I-356 15 minutes), fees, and states petitioners/obligors should already possess expertise to complete forms; familiarization costs are accounted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) — required element: identification of relevant Federal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 5. An identification of all relevant Federal rules, to the extent practical, that may duplicate, overlap, or conflict with the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states it is unaware of duplicative, overlapping, or conflicting Federal rules, addresses relationship to PRWORA elsewhere in the preamble, and invites comments on any such rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) — required element: alternatives minimizing impact
rubrics_metrics.description: 6. Description of any significant alternatives to the proposed rule that accomplish the stated objectives of applicable statutes and that minimize any significant economic impact of the proposed rule on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS considered a 'no action' alternative (continue 1999 Guidance) and a broader definition of 'public benefit' including more non-cash benefits; chose a more limited list of high-expenditure non-cash benefits to enhance administrability and predictability and potentially reduce overall transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) timing for major rule
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule is a major rule as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804 (Congressional Review Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enacted as final, the rule would be effective at least 60 days after the date on which Congress receives the report submitted by DHS under the CRA, or 60 days after the final rule’s publication, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) applicability threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Title II of UMRA requires a written statement assessing effects of any Federal mandate that may directly result in a $100 million or more expenditure (adjusted for inflation) in any one year by governments or the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inflation-adjusted value of $100 million in 1995 is approximately $161 million in 2017. DHS determined this proposed rule does not contain such a mandate, so UMRA Title II does not apply; DHS invites public comment if commenters believe otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule will not have substantial direct effects on the States, on the relationship between the National Government and the States, or on distribution of power/responsibilities among levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because DHS does not expect substantial direct compliance costs on State/local governments or preemption of State law, no federalism summary impact statement is warranted under EO 13132 section 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12988 (Civil Justice Reform) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule meets the applicable standards set forth in sections 3(a) and 3(b)(2) of Executive Order 12988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO 12988 concerns drafting of regulations to minimize litigation and establish clear legal standards; DHS affirms conformity to these standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 (Tribal consultation) threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule does not have tribal implications under EO 13175 because it would not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on distribution of power/responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS thus determines consultation/coordination under EO 13175 is not required for this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family assessment under Treasury Appropriations Act section 654
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS reviewed the proposed rule under section 654(c)(1) and determined the proposed rule may decrease disposable income and increase poverty of certain families and children, including U.S. citizen children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS states that, for reasons in the preamble, the benefits of the action justify the financial impact on families, and notes the proposed action would expand the list of public benefits considered for inadmissibility, potentially increasing the number of aliens found inadmissible under section 212(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA categorical exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For an action to be categorically excluded under DHS Instruction 023-01-001 Rev. 01, the action must satisfy each of the following: (1) the entire action clearly fits within one or more of the Categorical Exclusions; (2) the action is not a piece of a larger action; and (3) no extraordinary circumstances exist that create the potential for a significant environmental effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS analyzed the action, concluded NEPA does not apply due to excessively speculative nature of environmental impact analysis; nevertheless, if NEPA applied, the action would fall within categorical exclusion A.3(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) submission requirement and forms summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, agencies are required to submit to OMB for review and approval any reporting requirements inherent in a rule; Table 57 summarizes forms that are part of this rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 57 lists forms (I-129, I-129CW, I-356, I-485, I-539, I-693, I-864, etc.), whether they are new/updated, general purpose, filing categories, and applicability to public charge (e.g., updates adding questions/instructions about receipt of public benefits; USCIS may request Form I-944).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms applicability and evidentiary roles in public charge determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific forms are updated or used in public charge analysis: e.g., I-129/I-129CW updates add questions about receipt of public benefits; I-356 requests cancellation of public charge bond; I-485 applicants generally must be admissible including regarding public charge; I-539 updated to add questions about receipt of public benefits; I-693 used for the Health Factor; I-864 (Affidavit of Support) is a factor in the public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PRA table includes applicability notes: EOS/COS applicants may be required to file I-944 at USCIS discretion; the I-693 informs the Health Factor; the Affidavit of Support, when required, is considered in the public charge determination; some forms were discontinued or revised (I-864W incorporated into I-485).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternatives (no-action and broader public-benefit definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS considered a 'no action' alternative (continue administering under 1999 Guidance) and a more expansive definition of 'public benefit' possibly including a broader range of non-cash programs; DHS chose a more limited list of high-expenditure non-cash benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS explains that the chosen approach is expected to reduce overall transfers compared to the broader alternative and enhance administrability and predictability, potentially producing cost savings for employers and surety companies versus a broader approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates of economic burdens on petitioners and surety companies
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the proposed rule would increase time burden by an additional 30 minutes on petitioners filing Form I-129 or I-129CW for EOS/COS, imposing direct costs; DHS estimated annual populations and resulting opportunity cost estimates (about $184 million for I-129 population and about $5 million for I-129CW population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS cannot estimate number of RFEs or exact number of surety companies that might be impacted. DHS estimates Form I-945 filing volume ~960 and Form I-356 ~25, notes nine surety companies posted immigration bonds in FY2015 and four of those were small entities; employers may incur labor turnover costs (assumed 20% of mean wage ~$10,124 per separated beneficiary). DHS invites public comments and data on these impacts.
